implementation_notes: The platform supplies the channel: any object can extend EventTarget, addEventListener registers a listener per event type, and dispatchEvent delivers the event to every registered listener - DOM events are this pattern. There is no registry to write; what remains is the delivery contract: listeners run synchronously in registration order, nothing is retained for offline subscribers, and listener lifetimes must be managed with removeEventListener.
pitfalls: Listeners are held by strong reference: forgetting removeEventListener leaks the subscriber for the lifetime of the target.
CustomEvent detail is untyped at the boundary; without a wrapper, publisher and subscriber can disagree about the payload without a compile error.
On the DOM a listener exception is reported but the remaining listeners still run - do not rely on that same behaviour in every runtime.

variants.name: node:events EventEmitter
variants.implementation_notes: The server-side realization: EventEmitter.on registers a listener and emit invokes all listeners for the event name synchronously, with once() for single-shot subscriptions and listener bookkeeping through listenerCount/removeListener. Use it for Node services (much of the core API is built on it); the EventTarget variant is the option when the same code also runs in browsers.
pitfalls: An exception thrown by one listener propagates and skips the remaining listeners for that emit; wrap handler bodies when isolation matters.
Emitting 'error' with no 'error' listener throws and can terminate the process.
Node warns past ten listeners per event (MaxListenersExceededWarning) as a leak signal; raising the limit hides exactly the bug it reports.
